Definition: , including the feminine ἥτις, and the neuter ὅτι from G3739 and G5100; which some, i.e. any that; also (definite) which same:--X and (they), (such) as, (they) that, in that they, what(-soever), whereas ye, (they) which, who(-soever). Compare G3754.
BiblicalUsage: hóstis means whoever, whichever, whatever. In Mark 4:20, the text says "And these are they which are sown on good ground."
TheologicalSignificance: In hóstis I find no hidden theology; it simply means whoever, whichever, whatever.
RelatedTopics: Word of God; Faith; Christian Life
RelatedEvents: The Parable of the Sower; The Magi Visit Jesus
